title: RBI Compounds Apollo Hospitals' FDI and FCCB Violations for Over Rs 17.7 Crore
case_name: In re Apollo Hospitals Enterprise Limited and five directors/officers (FEMA compounding)
citation: Compounding order dated June 2026, under Section 15, FEMA 1999
card_summary: The ED alleged four contraventions against Apollo Hospitals worth more than Rs 2,424 crore: FDI received in a prohibited sector without approval, FCCBs issued in breach of FEMA, and crossing the permitted FDI and shareholding caps. After an ED no-objection, the RBI compounded the violations, with the company paying Rs 17,76,80,121 and five directors, including Preetha and Suneetha Reddy, Rs 18 lakh each.
card_tip: Where FDI is received into a sector or above a shareholding cap needing prior approval, price compounding into the deal as a real cost; the payment here ran into crores even after settlement.
verification_notes: The four contraventions totalling over Rs 2,424 crore, the company's Rs 17,76,80,121 payment, the Rs 18 lakh payment by each of the five named directors/officers, and the mid-June 2026 compounding order are corroborated across Taxscan, The South First and The Federal reports; sources differ on whether the order issued 16 or 17 June 2026, so the later, more widely reported date is used.
